summary: M.S. in Computer Engineering, Rochester Institute of Technology, focused on embedded software and simulation-based validation. I validate control software virtually before it reaches hardware: an ADAS perception and control stack proven closed-loop in CARLA with zero collisions, Cortex-M4 bare-metal C firmware verified in Proteus before bring-up, and a full ABB workcell simulated end-to-end. Strong in embedded C/C++, Python test automation, UART/I2C/SPI bring-up, Linux, and Git/GitLab.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory test environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands in Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; root-caused and resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving Validation in CARLA
bullets: Validated a full perception and control stack in closed-loop CARLA simulation on Town02 with 30 vehicles and 10 pedestrians, achieving zero collisions and correct traffic-light compliance across multiple laps.
Built automated scenario and data generation pipelines using CARLA semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering, producing ~8,000 training frames with zero manual annotation.
Trained YOLO11n (mAP50 ~0.85) and fine-tuned UFLD (ResNet-18); integrated both into an adaptive control stack with lane-following and waypoint fallback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 monitoring firmware in bare-metal embedded C at 3.68 KB Flash and 1.58 KB RAM with a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus simulation before hardware bring-up.
Programmed peripherals directly at register level (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated a three-layer distributed control pipeline (mobile client, Flask-SocketIO Linux server, Jetson plus Arduino controller) over a WebSocket fabric; 100% pick reliability across 10 trials at ~11.5 s end-to-end latency.

Root-caused 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) across the Linux userspace and Arduino/AVR C++ firmware boundary; closed the grasp loop with dual VL53L0X ToF sensors on a TCA9548A I2C mux.

projects.name: ABB RobotStudio Automation Simulation
bullets: Designed and simulated a complete ABB workcell for a press-to-packing assembly pipeline, validating full-cycle repeatability virtually before deployment; programmed in RAPID with TCP socket pose acquisition and interrupt-driven bench logic.
